msgs.text: what's it cost to fine tune a small model to talk the way we want tex to

Less than you'd guess. For an open model in the 3-8B range, using a LoRA on a few thousand example chats: training runs are $5-15 each. You'll do several. The real cost is building clean examples of the voice you want, not compute.
what's a lora

A model is billions of numbers. Fine-tuning normally changes all of them. A LoRA freezes them and learns a small patch on top: megabytes, not gigabytes. Cheap to train, easy to swap, and the base model stays untouched.
could each user have their own

Yes, that's what LoRAs are good for. One base model, one tiny patch per user, and the server loads the right patch per request. The hard part is having enough of each user's messages, and getting their consent to train on them.
and serving cost vs just using haiku

About a wash at your size. A hosted 8B is about $0.20 per million tokens. Haiku is cheaper to read, pricier to write. I'd stay on Haiku with good examples now, and train once Tex has real conversations to learn from.
